intro.text: A lighteyed Alethi prince, son of Highprince Dalinar Kholin, who holds effective command of the Kholin army on the Shattered Plains and is known as a duelist.
Dalinar Kholin's son, a Shardbearer and celebrated duelist tasked with winning Shards from the other highprinces' champions.
The new highprince of House Kholin, who refused the Alethi crown, and husband of Shallan Davar.
Highprince of House Kholin and husband of Shallan, who leads a diplomatic mission into Shadesmar to win over the honorspren.

items.text: At five, Adolin visited his father on the battlefront with his mother and baby brother Renarin. Already energetic and fond of wooden swords, he saluted Dalinar shyly, told him that he and his mother prayed for his safety every night, and said he wanted to win a Shardblade himself rather than be given one.

Adolin began training with the sword at six. After refusing at first, he later took lessons from Zahel, and when he was young Dalinar had him serve two months in a spearman squad to learn what his men endured.
Unlike his father, Adolin was brought up and trained to be a highprince, and Dalinar believed this would make him a fine one.

On a chasmfiend hunt with King Elhokar and several highprinces, Adolin worried about his father's state of mind and reputation, and about Sadeas moving against him. He was dismayed to hear Dalinar consider leaving the Shattered Plains.

When the chasmfiend attacked, Adolin helped Dalinar and Elhokar kill it, awed by his father's prowess. He brashly defended Dalinar and Renarin against Sadeas's insults until Dalinar ordered him to stand down. Dalinar then set him to investigate whether the king's saddle girth had been cut deliberately, and asked him to respect Sadeas.

Adolin used a disastrous date with Janala to visit leatherworkers about the strap, and spoke with the ardent Kadash about Dalinar's visions. At a feast he reported his findings, admitted to dueling men who called the Kholins cowards, and agreed with Dalinar's plan to unite the highprinces in a strike on the Parshendi. Elhokar then handed the investigation to Sadeas.

Adolin was alarmed when Dalinar chose to trust Sadeas because of his visions, and argued with him about it. Sadeas joined a Kholin plateau run, and Adolin protected his father in battle. Afterward Dalinar kept pushing Adolin into leadership roles.

In Sadeas's warcamp, Adolin stopped one of Sadeas's officers from beating a prostitute and offered to escort her out of the camp. He then sent a nearby bridgeman, Kaladin, to deliver a message, tossing him a chip; Kaladin ignored the order.

Dalinar told his sons he meant to abdicate in Adolin's favor. Adolin thought it insane and argued that his father's visions were delusions, and was shocked to learn Dalinar had sought out the Old Magic. Warned by Wit, they braced for Sadeas to move against them, but Sadeas instead cleared House Kholin of suspicion.

After rescuing Dalinar and Sadeas on a joint plateau assault, Adolin won a duel against Resi and came to understand why his father followed the Codes. He begged Dalinar not to abdicate, and Dalinar agreed. Soon after, the family learned that Dalinar spoke an ancient language during his visions, proving they were real.

Adolin resolved to trust his father before the assault on the Tower. In the battle, Sadeas withdrew with all his bridges, abandoning the Kholin army. Adolin berated their decision to trust Sadeas, then apologized to Dalinar for fighting him on everything, and prepared to die beside him.

When a bridge crew returned, Kaladin ordered the wounded Adolin to pull his men back. Adolin resented a darkeyed bridgeman giving him orders, but obeyed. Back at Sadeas's camp, Dalinar told him not to summon his Blade and traded his own Shardblade for the bridgemen.

Adolin, banned from dueling until then, was tasked with winning Shards from other highprinces' Shardbearers. Before his first duel he confided his doubts to his Blade. He beat Salinor Eved brutally with Ironstance, angering the highjudge, and gave the won Blade to Renarin.

Adolin disliked and distrusted Kaladin. While sparring, he deliberately provoked Kaladin and threw him across the grounds, earning a rebuke from Zahel. He also goaded Kaladin into riding a difficult horse, then thanked him for not telling Dalinar.
On a plateau run, Adolin met the Parshendi warrior Eshonai, who knew his name and asked to meet Dalinar. He then beat Eranniv in a duel, feigning a close fight to tempt other Shardbearers.

When the Assassin in White attacked the palace, Adolin fought beside Dalinar and Kaladin but was Lashed to the ceiling and knocked out of the fight. Afterward he grew suspicious of how well Kaladin had fared, noting his supposedly cut arm was unharmed.

Adolin hooked Elit Ruthar into a duel and nearly punched Sadeas. He was then taken with the newly arrived Shallan Davar, who reported that Jasnah had died. After some flirting, their causal betrothal was confirmed.

On their first outing, Shallan's frank questions made Adolin's conversation more genuine. He admitted he wasn't as dense as he pretended, promised to get her onto the Plains to study a chasmfiend chrysalis, and shared his father's visions and Sadeas's betrayal.

Disguised as Dalinar in Renarin's Plate, Adolin met Eshonai, who told him the Parshendi now sought the Alethi's destruction rather than peace. He then won Elit's Shards by draining his Plate of Stormlight, and goaded Relis into a duel against Adolin and any partners he brought.

In the duel, Adolin faced four Shardbearers. Unable to yield, he fought on as Renarin joined and was threatened. Kaladin joined too, and together they defeated the others. Adolin asked the king for the Right of Challenge against Sadeas, but Kaladin interrupted to challenge Amaram, and the chance was lost.
When Kaladin was imprisoned, Adolin locked himself in a cell in solidarity. He readily believed Kaladin about Amaram and offered him a set of Shards, which Kaladin gave to Moash instead.

Adolin arranged an expedition so Shallan could study a chasmfiend chrysalis, and told Kaladin he trusted him. When a carpenter destroyed their bridge, Adolin saved his father but could not stop Shallan and Kaladin from falling into the chasms. After they returned, he rushed to Shallan, and they kissed.

In the Battle of Narak, Parshendi lightning killed Adolin's Ryshadium, Sureblood. Remembering Shallan's remark that the rock formations were hollow, he led a thousand men through one to strike the singing Parshendi, sickened by the slaughter.

Adolin unwittingly grabbed the arm of the Assassin in White, who beat him badly. Even without Plate, he tried to defend Dalinar, but Szeth Lashed his father into the storm and broke Adolin's wrist. Kaladin then returned with Dalinar safe.

Learning Kaladin was a Radiant, Adolin laughed that he had known something was off. On Shallan's plateau he discovered she was a Radiant too, and they used her spren as a Blade to activate the Oathgate, carrying everyone to Urithiru.

Adolin led the mapping of Urithiru. When Sadeas told him he would take everything from Dalinar, Adolin snapped and killed him, then hid the evidence and rejoined his scouts as if nothing had happened.

Keeping his role in Sadeas's death secret, Adolin was put in charge of training the armies, attended Dalinar's wedding, and was then assigned to investigate Sadeas's murder and a copycat killing. Visiting Dalinar's neglected Ryshadium, Gallant, he talked with Renarin about his brother's emerging powers, and Renarin healed his wrist.

Adolin visited Shallan, who formally introduced Pattern, and offered to teach her the Shardblade. During his investigation, Ialai Sadeas pointed him toward the Kholin troops. When Ialai named Amaram regent of the Sadeas princedom, Adolin was furious, and he told Shallan that Kaladin had killed her brother Helaran.
When Shallan found the lair of a malevolent spren beneath the tower, Adolin led Bridge Four soldiers and Renarin down to face it, trusting Shallan's judgment as she fought and defeated it.

Kaladin flew Adolin, Shallan and Elhokar to Kholinar, where they slipped into the city in disguise and hid at Adolin's tailor's house. Adolin and Elhokar courted support among the local lighteyes, and Adolin acted as Kaladin's handler while he infiltrated the Wall Guard.

Adolin helped storm the palace and freed loyal guards, but reached Kaladin only after Elhokar had been killed. Seeing that Kholinar was lost, he ordered a retreat and had Shallan activate the Oathgate despite the trap, sending them into Shadesmar.

In Shadesmar, Adolin met the deadeye spren of his Shardblade and felt useless without skills to help. A talk with Azure about duty made him reflect on his role. Fleeing Fused-held Celebrant aboard an honorspren ship, he confessed to Shallan that he had killed Sadeas.

Attacking the Fused guarding Thaylen City's Oathgate, Adolin was run through with a lance and survived only because his Blade's deadeye spren attacked. Dalinar then opened a way back to the Physical Realm.

Healed by Renarin, Adolin rallied the defense of Thaylen City and fought a thunderclast. His Blade spoke her name, Mayalaran, into his mind, and he summoned her faster than usual. Afterward he offered to step aside for Kaladin, but Shallan chose him.
Adolin refused Dalinar's offer of the Alethi throne, confessed to killing Sadeas, and agreed to become highprince of House Kholin. He and Shallan married soon after.
Seven months after Thaylen Field, while fighting in Jah Keved, Adolin threw Maya and resummoned her in under ten heartbeats.

Adolin and Shallan led a mission against the Sons of Honor, with Adolin shadowing her as she let herself be kidnapped. They captured Ialai, but she was found murdered, and Adolin was horrified when Shallan's Veil persona suggested that killing her would not have been so bad.

Adolin dragged a depressed Kaladin to Jez's Duty after he was relieved of duty. He admitted wanting to help Kaladin and Shallan without knowing how, which helped Kaladin see that Adolin was already helping him. He refused to give up Maya for a living Blade.

After a coalition meeting, Shallan volunteered to lead a mission to the honorspren with Adolin. Before leaving, Adolin and Dalinar argued over expectations; Adolin realized he could not forgive his father for his mother Evi's death, though Dalinar voiced confidence in him.

In Shadesmar, Adolin cared for Maya, who began helping brush Gallant and joined him in a new kata. At the town of Nameless they met Notum, the honorspren captain exiled for helping them before, who warned that the honorspren would turn them away.

On the road, Shallan's personas told Adolin she feared he would leave over her secrets; he insisted he never would. Realizing that a Tukari band had been following Notum, Adolin rode to his rescue and fought off around twenty attackers, with Maya standing back to back with him.
At Lasting Integrity the honorspren shredded the monarchs' letters and refused the envoy. Desperate, Adolin offered to stand trial for humanity's past, and they let him in.
Imprisoned for weeks, Adolin studied honorspren law with the inkspren Blended and requested a trial by witness. The judge turned out to be the Herald Kelek, who seemed biased against him.

At the trial, witnesses argued that humans would always betray spren, though Notum shouted that Honor lived in men's hearts. Adolin argued humans could improve, but the honorspren turned the crowd against him with the deadeye Cryptic.

On the final day, the new judge Sekeir made Maya the last witness. As she grew distraught, Adolin shared his strength with her, and she spoke out, revealing that Radiants and spren had chosen together to break their bonds. Blended acknowledged a bond between Adolin and Maya.
Afterward, Adolin watched Shallan use her Seon to tell Mraize she was leaving the Ghostbloods, and reassured her they could handle the consequences.
During the Battle of Azimir, Adolin lost his right leg below the knee.

appearance.text: Adolin has blond hair streaked with black, inherited from his mother, worn in a stylish mess; blue eyes; and a handsome, clean-shaven face. He is lighter-skinned than his father and shorter than Kaladin.

personality.text: Adolin is fiercely loyal to his father yet unafraid to voice disagreement. Skeptical of the Codes of War at first, he comes to understand them and grows as a leader. He is not especially religious.

Adolin is confident, charismatic and friendly with lighteyes and darkeyes alike, though close to few, and is known for many short-lived courtships. He cares deeply for his family, defends Renarin readily, and carries his late mother's chain for luck in duels.

Adolin has a strong sense of right and wrong and a hot temper, willing to kill those he sees as threats to his loved ones. He is observant and slow to trust those he suspects, and more tactically minded than he lets on, sometimes feigning denseness.

As highprince, Adolin struggles to find his place among Radiants and feels he has little to offer without Surgebinding, which drives him to prove himself. He is a caring friend who notices when others need support.
